analysis.title: Califoreboding / US Economy and Iran War Tracker
key_insights: California has the third highest state GDP growth over the last year at 3.6%, behind only New York and Idaho, largely attributable to AI, despite energy costs about 50% above the national median, the highest state unemployment rate at 5.1% and the least affordable home ownership market.

A basket of 42 AI stocks accounts for 60%-80% of S&P 500 earnings growth, price returns and capital spending since January 2024. The chart shows 67% of price return, 58% of earnings growth and 81% of capex/R&D growth.

Market breadth is narrow: 60% of S&P 500 stocks are down 20% or more from their all-time highs while the index is near its high. Only 30% of stocks are outperforming the S&P 500 on a 3-year trailing basis, one of the lowest readings since 1991.

AI is benefitting AI supply chain companies more than the companies adopting it. The chart tracks trailing 12-month earnings for the AI supply chain (55 companies) against high, medium and low AI adopter groups.
Technology's share of US GDP growth has risen from almost zero through 2022 to about 33%. Only 20% of US states are growing faster than the national average, almost the lowest share since 1979.

AI-related construction (data centers and power) is up 38% since January 2024 and is the only positive category in US construction spending. Manufacturing is down 28%, commercial real estate down 13% and residential down 6%. A decline in planned data centers is flagged as something to watch.

Net interest costs are still at an all-time low share of US corporate profits despite higher short-term rates. Cembalest says the corporate sector appears more immune to rising short-term rates than in the past, at least so far.

Since January 2024, tech stocks globally have been driven mostly by earnings growth rather than P/E multiple expansion. Cembalest says markets driven by earnings growth are less susceptible to rapid declines than those driven by multiples.
SpaceX is holding up better than most large tech IPOs at day 116 after listing, but only about 20% of its shares have been released into the free float, so it may be too early to judge.
Chinese auto brands are gaining share in Europe even with 17%-35% tariffs. VW plant data shows manufacturing labor cost per hour of €74 in Emden, €37 in Palmela and €12 in Tianjin.

Europe is reportedly prepared to impose its own Section 301-style tariffs on China if China does not meet EU demands. China exports more rare earths and permanent magnets to Germany alone than to the US and has opened anti-dumping investigations into European exports.

Anthropic reports that Z.AI's open weight model GLM 5.3 was 'abliterated' for under $5,000, which cut its refusal rate on harmful requests to almost 0% with no loss in performance. GLM 5.3 costs about $2.00 per task versus $7.63 for Claude Fable 5.1. Cembalest reads the report as a pre-IPO push by Anthropic for regulation of competitor open weight models.

The 10-year Treasury yield has broken through the level set by the August 19 Twist operation. Cembalest attributes the rise to sticky inflation, hyperscaler debt issuance and above-expectation GDP growth, not a 'Final Act' for the debt.

For the first time since 1970 the US budget deficit is worse than 5% of GDP and deteriorating during an economic expansion. CBO projects 100% of federal tax revenues will be needed for entitlements and interest by 2030-2031.

Cembalest considers an eventual budget restructuring (tax increases and mandatory spending cuts, many means-tested) more likely than outright Fed debt monetization, which he says would be positive in the long run.

Private credit stress depends on the definition. Providers such as KBRA, Lincoln, S&P, Houlihan Lokey and Proskauer cite default rates of 1%-3%. Cliffwater's measure (non-accruals plus PIK loans with fair value of 96 or below) shows about 5%, and JPMAM's BDC loan analysis shows about 15%.

Realized losses and write-offs in private credit remain low, below 1% in Cliffwater data and 1%-2% in the JPMAM BDC analysis. Cliffwater data show 70% of amended PIK loans never fully return to cash pay two years later.
Cembalest does not expect the 2026 US midterms to have substantial near-term impacts on financial markets, whatever the outcome.

sector_views.rationale: Tech multiples are not cheap, but returns since January 2024 came mostly from earnings growth rather than multiple expansion. Concentration in AI supply chain names is a risk.
Chinese brands are taking share in Europe because of large plant cost gaps, and tariffs of 17%-35% have not slowed imports. European deindustrialization is a concern.

earnings_insights: The 42-stock AI basket accounts for 58% of S&P 500 earnings growth since January 2024 (JPMAM/Bloomberg, Oct 7, 2026).
Trailing 12-month earnings of the S&P 500 AI supply chain group (55 companies) have outpaced the AI adopter groups, per Bloomberg, MIT FutureTech and JPMAM data through Q2 2026.

macro_indicators.interpretation: First time since 1970 that the deficit is above 5% of GDP while the economy is expanding (manufacturing PMI above 50 and unemployment below NAIRU).
Highest state unemployment rate in the US.
Third highest among states behind New York and Idaho, largely attributable to AI.

macro_indicators.indicator: Federal revenue needed for entitlements and interest
macro_indicators.interpretation: CBO projection. Cembalest says something may have to give by then, possibly after a bond market riot, a rating downgrade and weaker foreign official demand.

macro_indicators.indicator: Technology share of US GDP growth
macro_indicators.interpretation: Up from almost zero through 2022, showing growth concentration in AI-related investment.

macro_indicators.indicator: Corporate net interest costs as share of after-tax profits
macro_indicators.interpretation: Corporate profits have not been hit by higher short-term rates the way past cycles suggest.
Non-accruals plus PIK loans with fair value of 96 or below, divided by total loans.
Broader definition including distressed PIK, maturity extensions, equity conversions and loans marked below 80.

risk_factors: Concentration of S&P 500 returns, earnings growth and capex in a small group of AI stocks.
A decline in planned data centers, since AI is the only growing construction category.
Rising 10-year Treasury yields alongside a deficit above 5% of GDP in an expansion, with possible bond market stress, a rating downgrade and reduced foreign official demand.
Private credit stress that is higher under broader definitions (about 5% to 15%), with 70% of amended PIK loans not returning to cash pay.
European deindustrialization and Chinese auto share gains, plus EU-China trade escalation involving rare earths.
Cyber risk from open weight AI models that can be stripped of safety controls cheaply, and possible regulation.
Lockup expirations for the SpaceX IPO, with only about 20% of shares in the free float.
charts_described: Chart of the cost of energy per mmbtu in California versus the mix cost elsewhere, with California above the 80th percentile state (WA) and the median (GA)
Bar chart showing the 42 AI stock basket's share of S&P 500 price return (67%), earnings growth (58%) and capex/R&D growth (81%)
Chart of the 10-year US Treasury yield from Jan 2026 to Sep 2026 marking the August 19 Treasury Twist operation announcement
Chart of Cliffwater private credit stress levels, with stress at about 5% and realized losses below 1%
PitchBook chart of BDC shadow defaults by type, with stress near 15% of loans
vol_and_positioning: Market breadth is weak: 60% of S&P 500 stocks are more than 20% below their all-time highs while the index is within 1% of its high, and only 30% of stocks are outperforming the index on a 3-year trailing basis.
The 42-stock AI basket drives 67% of price return since January 2024, so index-level positioning is heavily tied to one trade.
geopolitical: Europe is reportedly prepared to impose its own Section 301-style tariffs on China if China does not agree to voluntary export restrictions, predictable rare earth export licenses, reduced overcapacity and better market access.
China has begun anti-dumping investigations into European exports as EU-China trade tensions escalate.
The report is titled as an Iran War Tracker, but this issue's text does not discuss the Iran war.
US midterms in 2026 are expected by Cembalest to have little near-term market impact.
cross_bank_references: Goldman Sachs is cited as the source for the data on Chinese auto brands' market share gains in Europe (July 2025 to July 2026).
Gavekal Research is cited for China's rare earth and permanent magnet exports to Germany versus the US.
Cliffwater Research is cited for the ~5% private credit stress measure.

tension_points.bull_case: Tech stocks have been driven mostly by earnings growth rather than multiple expansion since January 2024, which Cembalest says makes markets less susceptible to rapid declines.
tension_points.bear_case: A basket of 42 AI stocks accounts for 60%-80% of S&P earnings growth, price returns and capex, 60% of S&P stocks are down 20% or more from highs, and AI is the only growing construction category.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A decline in planned data centers, which the report says is something to watch.

tension_points.theme: Rising Treasury yields and federal debt
tension_points.bull_case: The yield rise reflects sticky inflation, hyperscaler debt issuance and above-expectation GDP growth, not a 'Final Act' for the debt. Budget restructuring is judged more likely than debt monetization.
tension_points.bear_case: The deficit is above 5% of GDP in an expansion, and CBO projects all federal revenue goes to entitlements and interest by 2030-2031.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A bond market riot combined with a rating agency downgrade and reduced foreign official demand for Treasuries.

tension_points.bull_case: Realized losses and write-offs are low (below 1% at Cliffwater, 1%-2% at JPMAM) and several providers cite default rates of 1%-3%.
tension_points.bear_case: Broader stress measures show about 5% (Cliffwater) to about 15% (JPMAM BDC universe), and 70% of amended PIK loans do not return to cash pay.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Greater price discovery on stressed positions that turns marks into realized losses.

theme_stances.key_argument: A small basket of AI stocks drives most S&P earnings growth, returns and capex while market breadth is weak.
theme_stances.evidence: a basket of 42 AI stocks accounts for 60%-80% of all S&P earnings growth

theme_stances.key_argument: Stress depends on definition, and broader measures show 5%-15% against reported default rates of 1%-3%.
theme_stances.evidence: measuring private credit stress is both art and science

theme_stances.key_argument: The yield rise reflects sticky inflation, hyperscaler debt issuance and strong GDP, not the start of a debt crisis.
theme_stances.evidence: I don't think the "Final Act" is underway now
